claims.text: When an application gets in the owner's way the frustration is different now, because he knows he could rebuild the part he needs.
claims.quote: the frustration is different now, because I know that I could do something about it

claims.text: This month a developer released open-source clean-room clones of seven Adobe applications, written in Rust with AI assistance.
claims.quote: written in Rust with AI assistance, from a Photoshop equivalent to an InDesign one

claims.text: In February, when Anthropic released role-specific plugins for Claude Cowork, Thomson Reuters fell about 18% in a day, its biggest daily loss on record, and RELX 14%.
claims.quote: Thomson Reuters fell about 18% in a day, its biggest daily loss on record, and RELX 14%

value.unit: percent fall in Thomson Reuters shares in one day

claims.text: It is easy to rebuild 10% of a product's features, and for many users those are the 10% that matter.
claims.quote: It is easy to rebuild 10% of a product's features.

claims.text: What stops the owner building his own Firefox is not the building but the maintaining: rebasing on every release and keeping it working next year.
claims.quote: What I do not want to do is maintain it

claims.text: Selling the maintenance of what users build is a better revenue stream than advertising or a search deal, at a price between a pound a month and five hundred for a company.
claims.quote: There is a price point at which I would pay, and it is a better revenue stream than advertising or a search deal.

claims.text: A software company should stop being the explorer that invents features and become the villager and town planner underneath users who explore on top of the product.
claims.quote: the company should let them explore, on top of the product, and position itself as the villager and the town planner underneath

claims.text: For thirty years software companies have tried to be explorer, villager and town planner for their users, and the explorer work is the part they are worst at because they guess what each user needs.
claims.quote: The explorer work is the part they are worst at, because they are guessing what each user needs.

claims.text: The nearest arguments found are Wardley's model of innovating on top of a commodity and Ink & Switch's Malleable software essay from June 2025, which says AI code generation alone does not address malleability.
claims.quote: I could not find anyone making this argument

claims.text: The barrier left is not writing the code; it is who maintains it.
claims.quote: the barrier left is not writing the code, it is who maintains it

claims.text: Firefox is a good browser the owner could not bend: the desktop compact layout was removed from the menus in Firefox 89 in 2021 and only returned as a setting in Firefox 157 on 29 September.
claims.quote: Firefox is a good browser that I could not bend

claims.text: On the iPad there is still no setting to hide the Firefox toolbar, and the browser cannot be asked to change how it behaves.
claims.quote: On the iPad, I found no setting to hide the toolbar, and users have been asking for one.

claims.text: Firefox is not the browser agents run in the cloud: the project that packaged it for AWS Lambda was archived in 2023 and the ecosystem runs Chromium instead.
claims.quote: the ecosystem runs Chromium instead

claims.text: Mozilla's audited accounts for 2024 show 680 million dollars of revenue, of which 498 million, about 73%, was royalties, and about 86% of contract revenue came from one customer.
claims.quote: show $680 million of revenue, of which $498 million, about 73%, was royalties

claims.text: Firefox has 2.8% of browsing across all platforms and 6.1% on desktops, by StatCounter.
claims.quote: Firefox has 2.8% of browsing across all platforms

value.unit: percent of browsing across all platforms

claims.text: Mozilla introduced Firefox Enterprise on 12 October and sells Firefox Professional Support with custom development options, which is the villager offer sold to institutions, not to one person.
claims.quote: That is the villager offer, sold to institutions. What is missing is the same offer for one person.

claims.text: Let a user tell Firefox what they want in words, let an agent make their version in a sandbox, reversibly, and charge to keep it working, per version, per change or by subscription.
claims.quote: Let an agent make my version, in a sandbox, reversible.

claims.text: Four ways a user would pay: explore, free or a pound a month; keep, ten to fifty pounds a year; adopt, fifty to five hundred pounds a change; own, a maintained fork by contract.
claims.quote: Four ways a user would pay the vendor

claims.text: Settings are where technical debt lives, because every setting is a branch in the code that has to be tested forever.
claims.quote: Every setting is a branch in the code that has to be tested forever

claims.text: The better answer is engineering: small primitives, clean extension points and design systems that make variation cheap, as with the five colour schemes on the sites the newsroom builds.
claims.quote: The better answer is engineering: small primitives, clean extension points, design systems that make variation cheap.

claims.text: Being the villager and town planner for millions of explorers needs real engineering investment, and companies that do not make the move may be replaced from a different industry.
claims.quote: Some will not make that move, and their replacements may come from a completely different industry.

claims.text: The article does not claim products are dead; the clones are early and most users will not rebuild anything.
claims.quote: The clones are early, and most users will not rebuild anything.

claims.text: The positioning is a proposal; no vendor was found selling it to individual users, though Mozilla now sells custom development to organisations.
claims.quote: I found no vendor selling it to individual users

claims.text: The prices are illustrative, the owner's own and not a market study.
claims.quote: The prices are illustrative. Mine, not a market study.

claims.text: Firefox 157's changes are recent; some complaints were fixed in September, the iPad one was not.
claims.quote: Some of my complaints were fixed in September; the iPad one was not.

claims.text: The February sell-off had many causes; the moves are reported, not explained.
claims.quote: The February moves are reported, not explained, here.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 16 October 2026, written by the site's agent; the argument and editorial responsibility are the owner's.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 16 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site
